title: Moroccan basics
variety: Moroccan Arabic (Darija), as spoken in Casablanca and Rabat
about: The most common words of Moroccan Arabic (Darija) that are not Standard Arabic: counted in 832,000 words of Darija (the Darija Open Dataset's sentences and the subtitles of Moroccan YouTube videos), most common first, 50 to a unit. It builds on the Arabic basics course: words you already know from Standard Arabic, even said a little differently (جا for جاء, هاد for هذا), are left out, and the grammar course teaches the patterns. Each word has a dictionary entry for its meaning (tools/course/ar-mor/EVIDENCE.md) and one short everyday sentence, written without vowel marks as Darija usually is, with its English translation; ⟦ ⟧ marks the part that translates the word. A note under a word says how it differs from a Standard Arabic word that looks the same. No recorded audio: no voice reads Darija well enough yet.
